slides.title: Segmentation methods in context
rows: Transparent baseline with sensitivity to gain and artifacts
Candidate supervised baselines once expert masks are available
A bounding box produces an initial region proposal
slides.foot: Our implementation combines a pretrained promptable model with local texture refinement.
slides.notes:
Classical methods use explicit intensity or boundary assumptions. Supervised networks learn a task from labeled examples. U-Net and nnU-Net provide established biomedical segmentation approaches. MedSAM adapts SAM to medical images and uses bounding-box prompts. The MedSAM paper reports training on 1,570,263 image-mask pairs across ten modalities. Ultrasound-specific adaptations such as SAMUSA are relevant future comparison candidates. We have implemented the MedSAM-plus-texture workflow here. A new supervised Clarius model has not yet been trained.

labels: Variable interfaces and field of view
slides.foot: Speckle, low contrast, and acquisition settings complicate consistent boundaries.
slides.notes:
These are actual full-frame MATLAB exports from the local data. Describe the visible appearance without assigning a diagnosis. Speckle and shadows can make texture or intensity alone ambiguous. Neighboring structures can have similar brightness. In the local experiments, this ambiguity contributed to broad MedSAM masks, lower-boundary spillover, and missed tissue during refinement. Window size and quantization also change what the texture descriptors summarize.

slides.title: Image processing in MATLAB
steps: Archive preparation
Python extracts and decompresses unchanged RAW frame bytes.
B-mode samples
MATLAB reads the recorded uint8 *_env.raw stream.
Selected display mapping
MATLAB applies gamma 0.8 and full-frame bilinear resizing.
Model input
MATLAB writes 1418 × 853 PNGs with source metadata.
slides.foot: The sample grid requires further scan-conversion and physical-spacing verification.
slides.notes:
The active export pipeline assigns archive extraction, LZO decompression and timestamp-based frame selection to Python. MATLAB reads the array, applies the pointwise gamma curve, resizes the complete frame and writes PNGs. The recorded ENV stream is already B-mode grayscale, so it should not receive a second Hilbert transform or logarithm. The exported 1418 by 853 grid is a display grid. It does not establish calibrated millimeter spacing or reproduce every part of the Clarius website display pipeline. Historical RF-derived images remain relevant to interpreting the earlier results.

slides.foot: Matched capture timestamps. RF and B-mode are distinct acquisition streams.

slides.title: MedSAM and local refinement
steps: Bounding-box prompt
The user draws a box around the target.
MedSAM proposal
The pretrained model produces a parent mask.
Local appearance maps
Brightness statistics and GLCM or GLSZM describe tissue within that mask.
Automatic selection
An automatic seed guides recovery and spatial cleanup.
slides.foot: The final region stays inside the MedSAM parent. Missed parent-mask tissue remains a limitation.
slides.notes:
The workflow begins with a manual box prompt. The current checkpoint is the MedSAM ViT-B model. The model produces a broad parent mask, then the local refinement stage operates within that proposal. Interactive source-group inspection remains available, while the current Low / High variation mode automatically chooses a region. The automatic selector uses appearance compatibility and spatial rules. It has no trained liver-anatomy classifier. A parent mask that misses liver tissue constrains everything downstream. A parent-only baseline is therefore important in the planned evaluation.

slides.title: GLCM describes neighboring gray levels
lines: Quantize the image into 8 gray levels.
Count neighboring pairs within each masked window.
Calculate contrast, homogeneity, energy, and correlation.
Average four directions at two window scales.
slides.foot: Example directed counts for [0, 0, 1, 1]. The implementation also adds reverse pairs.
slides.notes:
A gray-level co-occurrence matrix counts how often a pixel of gray level i occurs beside gray level j at a chosen offset. The row [0,0,1,1] gives directed right-neighbor counts (0,0), (0,1), and (1,1). Our implementation symmetrizes and normalizes these counts. For the actual image, four directional features at half and full window scales yield eight maps. Both endpoints of a pair must be inside the parent mask and local window. GLCM can operate on rectangular images and irregular masked regions. The square matrix refers to the gray-level pair histogram. The feature counts are exact for the implemented windows and tested against scikit-image.

slides.title: Combined features and automatic selection
lines: Combined uses 4 brightness-statistic maps and 8 GLCM maps.
Clustering provides appearance groups. A compact, consistent group supplies the automatic seed.
Seed-derived brightness and texture ranges recover compatible tissue across groups.
Spatial cleanup limits thin extensions and preserves dark cavities.
slides.foot: Default q0.985 sets a seed-distance percentile for the texture gate.
slides.notes:
The two brightness scales each contribute a local mean and standard deviation. The two GLCM scales each contribute four descriptors. The original high/low-variation approach merged appearance colors and retained a large region. The current selector evaluates compact candidate bodies, penalizes local-intensity dispersion, and learns robust ranges from an automatic seed. It then recovers compatible tissue across source groups and applies opening, a bounded envelope, closing, cavity exclusion, and component selection. q0.985 refers to the 98.5th percentile of seed-normalized feature distance. For GLCM the gate uses the two correlation channels. It is not a raw correlation value of 0.985. Details are in the appendix.

slides.title: Local GLSZM as an alternative
rows: Exact sampled windows with feature interpolation
slides.foot: Both use 8 gray levels. GLSZM defaults to an 8-row × 2-column sampling step.
slides.notes:
A gray-level size-zone matrix records how many connected zones occur at each gray level and zone size. The implementation provides all sixteen standard ROI features. Local clustering uses eight descriptors per scale, including small- and large-area emphasis, normalized nonuniformities, zone percentage, variance measures, and entropy. Each sampled local window independently constructs zones. Intermediate feature values use mask-normalized bilinear interpolation. The default does not calculate a separate exact matrix at every native pixel. Quantization can split or merge zones, and large windows mix structures. The GLSZM appearance gate uses all sixteen local channels, so its q0.985 has a different feature-distance meaning from the GLCM gate.

slides.title: GLSZM sampling affects the selected region
rows: Dense features 3.38 s, sampled features 0.24 s
slides.foot: These checks show configuration sensitivity on the development data.
slides.notes:
The speed gain from sampling comes with an approximation. Feature RMSE here is divided by each dense feature’s fifth-to-ninety-fifth-percentile range on the patch. It is not a percentage of segmentation error. Changing from (8,2) to (4,1) altered the pure-GLSZM selection substantially on the outlined frame, while brightness-plus-GLSZM changed less. The finer full-frame extraction took 68.2 seconds. A small quantile sweep also failed to surpass the current method against that rough development outline. These observations support retaining GLSZM as an experimental alternative while evaluating it under a fixed, documented configuration.

slides.title: Remaining selection failures
labels: Pure GLSZM selects a deeper population
Brightness + GLSZM retains the upper region
slides.foot: Exam05 frame 003. Similar texture and seed choice can change the selected anatomy.
slides.notes:
Pure GLSZM switched to a deeper population on exam05 frames 003 and 010 in the saved comparison. Brightness-plus-GLSZM and Combined/GLCM were more consistent in selecting the upper region, although lower-left extensions persisted in some outputs. A largest-component rule cannot remove an incorrect extension that remains connected to the intended region. Large spatial windows can blur an internal boundary, and a dark-cavity rule can enlarge a shadow or miss a vessel. These are observed failure mechanisms and motivate targeted error review with the PI’s references.

slides.title: Evaluation on the PI references
steps: Fixed comparisons
MedSAM alone, brightness refinement, Combined / GLCM, GLSZM, and brightness + GLSZM.
Matched conditions
Use identical images, prompts, and saved parent masks for refinement comparisons.
Paired metrics
Report Dice, IoU, full-frame SSIM, ROI SSIM, precision, and recall.
Error review
Inspect missed liver, extra tissue, and lumen exclusions with runtime.
slides.foot: Keep development and evaluation groups separate at the patient or acquisition level when identifiers allow.
slides.notes:
This is a proposed evaluation protocol. Once the PI references are ready, freeze the preprocessing and method configurations before the comparison. A refinement-only comparison should reuse each saved MedSAM parent so the texture methods see the same initial proposal. A separate end-to-end analysis can expose parent-mask failures. Use identical reference domains across methods, report paired results, and include failed cases. Group repeated frames by examination or recording. Confirm patient identifiers before making patient-level split or sample-size claims. If parameters require tuning, use a separate development group and lock the final evaluation group. Compare native B-mode with gamma 0.8 within the same acquisition stream as a later preprocessing ablation.

slides.title: Longer-term lesion analysis
lines: Establish reliable liver regions first.
Study within-liver texture variation and repeatability.
Add expert lesion labels before testing lesion localization.
Consider task-specific training or ultrasound-adapted models.
slides.caption: Current work focuses on the liver region.
slides.notes:
The motivating future application is to highlight unusual regions within the liver. The current texture groups describe image appearance and are influenced by gain, shadows, speckle and scale. Lesion localization would require expert lesion annotations and its own evaluation, including false-positive and missed-lesion analysis. A liver ROI could restrict that future search and support region-level texture measurements. Repeated scans and acquisition metadata would help test feature stability. If enough expert references accumulate, compare a task-specific U-Net or nnU-Net and ultrasound-adapted promptable models with the current heuristic pipeline.

slides.title: Appendix · Current parameter settings
rows: MedSAM ViT-B with a user-drawn box
8 gray levels by default, CLI supports 16, 32, 64
slides.foot: Window sizes derive from the parent region. Display pixels have acquisition-dependent physical spacing.
slides.notes:
GLCM full windows are approximately one-eighth of the occupied parent height and width, capped at 129 rows by 33 columns, with odd sizes and a half-size second scale. Brightness-only retains the earlier quarter-mask window rule. Combined clustering weights after standardization are 1/sqrt(2) for each local mean, 0.25 for each local standard deviation, and 0.35/sqrt(8) for each GLCM channel. Brightness-plus-GLSZM distributes the texture weight as 0.35/sqrt(16). The selector uses a 256 by 256 normalized analysis grid for shape operations. These fixed heuristics still require validation across image grids.

slides.title: Appendix · Interpretation of the metrics
rows: Intersection / union of prediction and reference
Mean local structural similarity on binary 0/1 masks
Local SSIM averaged over a common evaluation domain
Retained foreground correctness and reference coverage
slides.foot: Report SSIM with overlap metrics because shared background can raise the full-frame score.
slides.notes:
SSIM uses data_range=1, eleven-by-eleven Gaussian windows, sigma 1.5, K1=0.01, K2=0.03 and population covariance. ROI mean SSIM is a custom summary of the SSIM map over the union of the parent, reference and every prediction, excluding invalid image-border centers. All methods use the same evaluation domain for an image. Full-array Dice and IoU directly describe foreground overlap. The current summary is a per-image macro mean and sample SD. Frame SD describes the sample spread and does not quantify independent-patient uncertainty. If physical boundary metrics are added, first verify sample spacing and scan conversion.
